newsitem.title: DENMARK: Copenhagen bourse turnover hits record in January.
newsitem.headline: Copenhagen bourse turnover hits record in January.

text.p: Share trading hit a monthly all-time high on Copenhagen Stock Exchange in January 1997, 63 percent up on the same 1996 month, the bourse said in a statement on Tuesday.
Share trading totalled 33.1 billion crowns in market value, an increase of 78 percent on the previous month, with average daily trading volume at 1.5 billion crowns, it said.
The previous monthly record of 28.6 billion crowns was set in January 1994.

Copenhagen Stock Exchange said industrial shares were the most traded during January 1997 with turnover of 11.6 billion crowns, followed by commerce and services at 8.7 billion crowns and banks at 6.7 billion crowns.

It said four shares achieved turnover in the month in excess of two billion crowns: Unidanmark at 2.6 billion crowns led the field, followed by Tele Danmark B at 2.4 billion crowns, Novo Nordisk B at 2.3 billion crowns and Den Danske Bank at two billion crowns.
It said share prices rocketed with the top-20 KFX index hitting 10 all-time record highs in the month to peak at 147.88 at end-January, 8.5 percent up on the beginning of the year.

Copenhagen Bourse said that nominal bond turnover in January amounted to 678.9 billion crowns, an increase of 33 percent on December 1996, but 24 percent down on January 1996. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
